_meta.notes: Per-archetype tailoring guidance for Placed's 'tailor my CV to this role' rewrite (UK undergraduate spring weeks, insight programmes, summer internships). Hard constraint above everything here: rewrite only what the source CV already says. No new facts, numbers, skills, employers or tools. No authorship escalation: a 'prefer' verb may replace a source verb only at the same or a lower level of the ladder familiar < used/assisted/supported/contributed < built/developed/implemented < led/managed/founded, and qualifiers ('helped', 'as part of a team of 4', 'coursework') must survive. A reframe applies only when its onlyIf condition is visibly met by the original line. Grades: A = employer's own guidance or several top UK careers services agree; B = one top-tier UK source (TARGETjobs, Prospects, a Russell Group careers service); C = practitioner or trade press (eFinancialCareers and consultants it quotes); D = our synthesis. Quotes are verbatim from pages fetched on 2026-10-14 (curly quotes and dashes normalised for matching), each 25 words or fewer. TF18, TF24 and TF29 were read via web.archive.org 2026 snapshots because the live sites blocked automated fetches; TF35 was not re-fetched and is carried over from docs/research/market-2026/02-recruiter-screening-evidence.md F16. Mapping to cv-rules-finance-consulting.md tags: TF1=S1, TF2=S2, TF3=S3, TF8=S8, TF14=S5, TF15=S6, TF18=S12, TF19=S15, TF20=S16, TF21=S14, TF22=S13, TF23=S17, TF24=S19, TF25=S22, TF26=S25, TF27=S26, TF28=S24, TF29=S23, TF30=S11-LSE brochure, TF32=S10. Caveat: Bain London asks candidates to use AI only to check CV grammar and spelling (TF29), so the product should tell users to check each target firm's AI policy.

finance_banking.summaryFormula: UK careers services and the TARGETjobs banking template omit a student profile because the cover letter or form does that job. Only when the CV already has one: shorten it to at most two lines of facts it already states (year, degree, university, and one or two finance signals the bullets already show). Leave out figures, any job title the student is applying for, and the grade. If the CV has no profile, leave it out: never write one. No adjectives.
